page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-32 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates that the single-core performance of this server is in the bottom 25 percent, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, its multi-core performance scales to average levels, placing in the middle 50 percent for multi-threaded tasks such as bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached reads and writes also performs in the average tier. Notably, the server demonstrates strong performance in the top 25 percent for text generation during LLM inference with small models, while prompt processing remains average.

Given its high vCPU count relative to memory, this server offers a compute-heavy profile. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require substantial parallel processing power without demanding large memory footprints. The lack of local storage and GPUs makes it less suitable for database-heavy or hardware-accelerated tasks. It is best suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, and text generation using smaller language models.
